successors.name: United Arab Emirates
successors.text: six of the seven Trucial sheikhdoms (Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah) united on 2 December 1971

ledger.x: 8 January 1820: the sheikhs of the coast sign the General Maritime Treaty with Britain.
6-8 March 1892: the Exclusive Agreement puts the rulers under British protection.
25 October 1955: the Trucial Oman Levies retake Buraimi.
29-30 November 1971: Iran seizes the Tunbs and Abu Musa.
2 December 1971: six Trucial States form the United Arab Emirates.

wars.name: Faisal's attacks on the Trucial States
wars.outcome: Faisal bin Turki 'attacked' the Trucial States in the 1860s and 'the British forces militarily stopped his attacks'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Buraimi Dispute
wars.outcome: Saudi guards occupied Hamasa on 31 August 1952; a Standstill Agreement (30 July 1954) and arbitration at Geneva (1955) failed; the Trucial Oman Levies retook the oasis on 25 October 1955.

wars.name: Iranian occupation of Abu Musa and the Tunbs
wars.outcome: Iran took the Tunbs by force and Abu Musa by a memorandum with Sharjah on 30 November 1971, two days before the UAE was proclaimed.

certainty.note: The 1820 and 1853 truces fix no boundaries; the sheikhdoms' limits are tribal and the inland frontier with Najd and Oman is undefined.
The Exclusive Agreement of 1892 fixes protection, not frontiers; the Buraimi frontier was settled only in 1974 (Treaty of Jeddah) and the island frontier with Iran never.

sources.title: Faisal bin Turki bin Abdullah Al Saud
